name: Atmospheric Survival
audience: Players who enjoy tension without losing navigational clarity.
camera: Third-person close-to-medium camera; hazards must read in low light.
identity: Ridge-cut shelters and wind-scarred slate create a distinct exposed-coast setting.

palette.rule: Use bright chroma sparingly; never communicate danger by darkness alone.

geometry: Broad shelter masses, broken but navigable edges and recognizable supply silhouettes.

materials.surfaces: Damp slate, rough timber and tarnished utility metal.
materials.texture_rule: Uneven weathering at drainage and touch points; maintain value hierarchy.
materials.tiling_rule: Ground repeats need seam checks and motif breakup at actual camera height.

lighting: Localized pools of practical light with accessible silhouettes and visible exit routes.
effects: Windborne flecks and limited fog; avoid masking hazards or degrading phone frame rate.
ui: Minimal inventory and strong status icons with text and non-color signals.
audio: Wind, shelter creaks and restrained low pulses; urgent warnings cut through ambience.

budgets.reuse_rule: Reuse shelter modules and weather overlays rather than unique high-resolution surfaces.

originality: Use original locations and survival symbols; exclude copied horror mascots, logos and recognizable level layouts.
